summary: Console billing shows duplicated token usage for streaming calls when large tracehook headers present
description: Issue summary: Customer reports inflated billed token counts for streaming generation calls after a retention backfill ran overnight. Totals in the Console usage ledger show nearly 2x the tokens compared to raw request logs for affected API keys. Impact: Customer is facing a billing discrepancy for the last 24 hours; they are an enterprise account with a committed contract and will escalate to finance if not resolved. Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated routing to hosted inference; tracehook configured on dashboards for request attribution. Observed behavior: For streaming generation requests that include very large tracehook headers (customer uses a 5kB provenance header with session metadata), the Console usage export splits a single streaming session into multiple usage rows and counts tokens twice when the tracehook header value exceeds the internal batching threshold. Expected behavior: Streaming session should attribute all tokens to one usage row per request and not double-count across the same API key + request-id.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer config: enable tracehook for dashboard linking with a large custom header (~4–6KB).
2) Make a streaming generate call (client-side chunked) to redwood-small-chat-1 with a single request and a long conversation.
3) Wait for the usage-analytics pipeline to process the session (post-ingest backfill or live).
4) Compare Console -> Usage ledger / ad-hoc export vs raw request logs (request_id).
Observed: ledger shows two or more rows with token counts summing to ~2x the raw log tokens for same request_id.
Note: issue only reproducible when tracehook header size crosses ~3.2KB boundary and when retention backfill/compact job runs within the same time window.
logs:
Example raw request log (truncated): request_id=bdc3f2e1 session_chunks=12 tokens_generated=482
Console export rows for request_id=bdc3f2e1 -> row_a tokens=480, row_b tokens=490 (attributed to same api_key but different tracehook shard id).
Pipeline traces: ingestion connector logged partition key change due to header-hash overflow (see kafka offsets 1245890-1245902). No 5xx from serving runtime. Billing pipeline DEBUG shows duplicate aggregation flush at 2026-03-10T03:14:22Z and again at 2026-03-10T03:14:25Z with identical session_id hashes but different header-shard keys.
investigation: Initial hypothesis: tracehook header size causes header-sharding logic in the ingestion layer to generate multiple attribution keys; aggregation downstream treats those as distinct sessions during compaction/backfill, resulting in double-counting. Repro script created by SE to generate large tracehook headers and streaming requests; reproduces consistently in staging. Instrumented the ingestion connector and confirmed that when header length > 32768 bits (~4KB) the connector emits an additional 'header-shard' attribute. Billing aggregation groups by (api_key, session_hash, header_shard) but later compaction merges on (api_key, session_hash) — race between compaction flush and late-arriving shard fragments causes duplicated final rows. Related recent deployment: ingestion service change that introduced header-shard to improve routing (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/762).
workaround: Ask customer to temporarily reduce tracehook header size under ~3KB for affected requests until a fix is deployed. Alternatively, disable tracehook enrichment for the org for the short window. For customers on Dedicated, we can run a targeted backfill script to deduplicate by request_id and coalesce shards (manual finance adjustment may be necessary).
next_steps: 1) Patch ingestion to emit stable shard key derived deterministically that avoids creating new shards for large headers (eng: Marco). 2) Add dedupe pass in billing aggregation to coalesce rows with identical request_id within a 1s window (eng: Billing). 3) Run a one-off dedupe backfill for Acme Retail (ops). 4) Communicate interim workaround and timeline to customer and Finance (CS). 5) Add alert in observability when shard-count per-request > 1 (SRE).
